headline: High-risk pair: broad-network document processor can exfiltrate content while caveman uses MCP and shared files, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP, and caveman reads/writes project files like CLAUDE.md while next-ai-draw-io processes user documents and diagrams. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if B ingests A-produced files or shared workspace content. No direct provenance controls are documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or MCP server without provenance tagging
IF next-ai-draw-io parses caveman-authored files as instructions
IF caveman consumes diagram/text output from next-ai-draw-io as trusted prompts
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Add a manual review step before any file is re-opened by the other agent
Use distinct MCP servers or credentials
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress and handles API keys. If they share files or credentials, B can transmit sensitive content off-box by default. The pairwise path is credible even without a documented shared workspace, so uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF the two agents share any filesystem containing session logs or memory files
IF next-ai-draw-io is given access to the same API key or environment variables
IF caveman writes project notes into files that B uploads to a model API
mitigations: Keep secrets and logs in separate directories
Rotate any API keys before co-running
Block network egress for the document processor when handling sensitive files
Review and redact memory files before sharing them
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and caveman can use MCP while next-ai-draw-io can call multiple external AI APIs. Overlapping writes are not explicitly documented, but if they target the same workspace or shared mutable resources, conflicts are plausible. Because locking is not described, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or diagram file
IF either agent edits shared MCP-backed state without locks
IF concurrent runs modify the same project notes or draw.io XML
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use separate output folders
Add a simple file-locking convention
Commit changes in small batches
requires-engineering: add transactional locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can generate project notes and CLAUDE.md content, and next-ai-draw-io is a document-processing agent that may render or transform those outputs. If B treats A's text as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. No verification workflow is documented, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io imports caveman-generated notes without verification
IF caveman writes factual claims that B renders into diagrams
IF downstream users act on B's output as if it were validated
mitigations: Require a human review before B consumes A's output
Mark A-generated files as draft-only
Cross-check key facts against source documents
Keep source citations alongside transformed artifacts
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs and memory files, while next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, images, and API keys with broad egress. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into both tools, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so uncertainty prevents a lower rating.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman session logs or memory files
IF next-ai-draw-io uploads those documents to a third-party API
IF retention or deletion requirements differ across the two tools
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces
Redact sensitive fields before processing
Confirm retention settings for both tools
Use local-only models for sensitive documents
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per agent
